candidates.title: The manual's slicing/splicing verification (cartesi.hash-tree verify_slice/verify_splice and the template-instantiation and result-extraction recipes) binds the proof neither to the known state hash M nor to the drive's address and size. A prover can make it accept any instantiated hash M', or a 'result' read from another node
candidates.component: Lua helper library cartesi.hash-tree (verify_slice, verify_splice, roll_hash_up_tree) and the manual's blockchain-perspective recipes doc/recipes/splice-calculator-with-new-drive.lua and doc/recipes/slice-calculator-output.lua (manual doc/README.md 'Slicing and splicing', 'Template instantiation', 'Result extraction', ~8237-8567)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'the Lua helper libraries' and the recipes outside the PRT referee model; no production deployment runs them). The library stands in for the role of the components that reach the defect through it. The PRT referee model (prt.lua validate_claim_response/validate_seal_response) and game-output.lua call verify_slice, but they check root_hash, target_address and log2 sizes themselves, so they do not reach the defect. The recipes stand in for the on-chain referee verifier that the manual describes as 'the blockchain way'.
candidates.location: src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua:31-45 (verify_slice compares the roll-up only with proof.root_hash, which the proof itself supplies. verify_splice = verify_slice(proof) + roll(new_target_hash) == new_root_hash, and checks neither target_address nor log2_target_size); doc/recipes/splice-calculator-with-new-drive.lua:26-33 (checks only template_input_proof.log2_root_size, never that proof.root_hash equals the template hash M, nor its target address or size); doc/recipes/slice-calculator-output.lua:30-39 (checks only output_proof.log2_root_size, never that output_proof.target_address == output_nvram.start or that log2_target_size == output_nvram.log2_size); manual doc/README.md 8322-8324, 8340-8351, 8417-8422, 8542-8552
candidates.description: The manual makes four promises here. (a) 'To verify a slicing operation, the code first checks the root hash M against the one found in the proof' (8340). (b) For splicing, 'First, the code verifies that the slicing operation is valid. This ensures that the sibling hashes are correct' (8345-8347). (c) For template instantiation, the blockchain can obtain M' from 'only the pristine input proof and the root hash of the modified input NVRAM' while it 'knows only the state hash M' (8246, 8417-8422). (d) For result extraction, passing 'the output proof, this reconstructed hash, and the agreed hash M' to verify_splice ... confirms that an output NVRAM with exactly this content sits in the machine whose state hash is M'' (8549-8552). The code does none of this. verify_slice never sees M: it checks only that the proof is consistent with its own proof.root_hash. So verify_splice accepts a proof whose siblings and root are fabricated, and the 'instantiated' hash it confirms is whatever the fabricator chose. Neither verify_splice nor either recipe checks proof.target_address or proof.log2_target_size against the drive, so the extraction check passes for any node of M' whose contents hash like the claimed result. For example, the input NVRAM holds bytes the instantiator chose, so the input expression can be 'extracted' as the computation's result. The extraction recipe also never authenticates that M' is halted or yielded (the analogue of A5's 'Extracting the root requires authenticating that status in the same state'). The recipes pass off-chain only because they recompute M' concretely and read the result from the right drive. The 'blockchain way' that the manual documents and attributes to this code is unsound.
candidates.trigger: A dishonest prover in the scenario the manual describes (a contract or verifier that knows only M or the agreed M', and that receives the proof and the result from a user). For instantiation, it submits a 'pristine input proof' with arbitrary siblings and root_hash = roll(siblings, arbitrary target). For extraction, it submits a whole-machine proof of another node of the same size (such as the input NVRAM) together with that node's contents as the 'result'.
candidates.reachability: No machine state is involved. The proof and the result are prover-chosen data, and section 4 says 'Logs and proofs are adversarial. A verifier must assume that every count, index, address, size, and hash it receives was chosen to fool it.' Reproduced with a synthetic machine (RAM plus two 4 KiB NVRAMs labeled input and output), with no guest code.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is adversarial proof data given to a verifier that follows the manual's recipe. That is not one of the exclusions: not ZK, not a validator node, not a test harness (the recipes are not *-test.lua), and it needs no snapshot, API misuse or deployment violation. 2. Role: Support. AUDIT.md lists 'the Lua helper libraries' as Support, and the recipes are demonstrations. Section 3: 'A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it.' The PRT referee model reaches verify_slice but checks root, address and sizes itself, so the most critical component that reaches this defect is the recipe standing in for the 'blockchain way' verifier. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier.' 3. High/Medium cases: Section 8 Medium lists 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium.' In the role it stands in for, a verifier, this is the soundness failure of section 1, 'a proof verifier accepts a node that the committed tree does not hold at the stated index and height'. R11 also says 'Every referee parameter comes from the referee, never from the proof' (index and height are referee parameters per section 2), and A5 says 'Extracting the root requires authenticating that status in the same state.' Each of these would be Critical in the referee-verifier role, so this is Medium. Section 8 also says: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual is right that the code checks M and confirms the output NVRAM, then the code is the defective support component, which again gives Medium. 4. Critical: not reached, because no component in a referee-verifier, referee-model or honest-operator role was found to reach the defect. Dave's LibMachineValidityProof and game-output.lua check addresses and sizes, but I did not audit Dave's code for this. 5. Alternative reading, Low: if the 'Hash-view of state' recipes count only as off-chain illustrations whose proofs are produced locally, with nothing standing in for a verifier, and the manual's 'blockchain way' prose counts as non-normative (the PRT referee model is the normative one), then this is 'a real defect that violates no rule' and is Low. Deciding fact: whether the manual's description of how 'the blockchain' verifies instantiation and extraction counts as a verifier specification that the recipes stand in for.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: a support defect that stands in for a referee verifier, together with a manual/code contradiction on a soundness point) / Low (if the recipes are read as off-chain illustrations only)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1: 'no adversary can make a correctly designed application ... accept an output that the settled state does not commit to.' A contract or verifier built as the manual says (the chain knows only M, and verify_splice 'confirms that an output NVRAM with exactly this content sits in the machine') accepts any instantiated hash that a forger picks, which is the wrong starting state of the computation. It also accepts as the computation's result any same-size node of the agreed state that the adversary controls, such as the input drive. The deployed PRT path is not affected, because game-output.lua and Dave's machine-validity proof bind root, address and size. The defect sits in the documented helper and its specification, which readers are told to reuse ('The data needed for the proofs ... verify_slice ... verify_splice').
candidates.evidence:
Ran scratch script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANHASHSTATE/splice-forge.lua with bugs/env.sh. (1) A forged pristine-input proof (52 arbitrary siblings, root_hash = roll_hash_up_tree of an arbitrary target; forged.root_hash ~= template M) passes the recipe's only check (log2_root_size == 64), and hash_tree.verify_splice(forged, input_hash, fake_M') succeeds, although fake_M' differs from the real instantiated hash. (2) After the output NVRAM is set to "2
", a whole-machine proof of the INPUT NVRAM (same log2 size 12) and the claimed result "1+1
" pass assert(log2_root_size == HASH_TREE_LOG2_ROOT_SIZE) and verify_splice(proof, get_data_root_hash("1+1
", 12), M2) against the agreed final hash M2, while the output NVRAM holds "2
". Output: 'instantiation: verify_splice accepts forged M': true  M' == real instantiated hash: false'; 'extraction: verify_splice accepts result "1+1
" from output nvram: true'.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: create the synthetic machine {ram 1 MiB, nvram input @0xa0000000 4 KiB, nvram output @0xb0000000 4 KiB}. Implement the manual's 'blockchain way' exactly as the recipes do: instantiate(M, proof, input) runs the recipe's checks plus verify_splice(proof, get_data_root_hash(input, 12), M'), and extract(M', proof, result) runs assert(log2_root_size == 64) plus verify_splice(proof, get_data_root_hash(result, 12), M'). Require, as the manual promises, that (1) a proof whose root_hash differs from M is refused and (2) a proof targeting the input NVRAM is refused when it is offered as the output NVRAM's proof. Exit 1 while either is accepted. It passes once verify_slice/verify_splice take the expected root, address and size (or the recipes check them) and the manual matches.

not_covered: Checked and found consistent (no candidate): get_proof for every log2_target_size 5..64 x log2_root_size target..64 at 15 base addresses (pristine gaps, shadow, PMAs, RAM edges, a non-power-of-2 flash drive's padding, tx buffer, top of the address space). root_hash, target_hash, sibling count, verify_slice, and the root matched get_node_hash and get_root_hash (27,450 cases; proofdiff.lua). Refusals of misaligned addresses and sizes <5 or >64 match the manual.

Checked and found consistent: the whole-machine root rebuilt from read_memory of every address range with an independent Lua Merkle composition and per-level pristine hashes matches get_root_hash under keccak256 and sha256. Device ranges (CLINT/HTIF/PLIC) hash as pristine. 1,500 random sub-range nodes (log2 5-16) per hash function match get_data_root_hash(read_memory) after random writes (fullroot.lua, nodediff.lua).

Checked: the cartesi-hash-tree-hash tool matches get_data_root_hash for 120 random (root, leaf, length, hash function) cases. Its diagnostics (log2_word_size not validated, root size 64 refused although the manual says nodes go up to 64) were judged Low tool issues and not reported.

Checked: the overlap and alignment checks of ranges rounded up to powers of 2 enforce the manual's 'each memory range is a complete subtree'. cartesi.keccak256/sha256 two-argument forms refuse non-32-byte inputs, so verify_slice cannot be fooled by sibling or target length tricks once more than zero siblings are rolled.

Checked: proof JSON/Lua serialization (to_json sibling order bottom-up, util.dump_table key order, CLI --initial-proof/--final-proof label lookup with ceil-log2 sizes). The CLI prose 'from the root all the way down to the target' (manual ~1539) is ambiguous about sibling order, but the Lua section and the code agree on bottom-up. Not reported.

Not covered: the JSON-RPC client's parsing of hash_tree_proof replies (ju_get_opt_field ignores extra sibling entries and allocates log2_root_size - log2_target_size siblings before checking the array; the server is trusted, already listed in context).

Not covered: whether the TLB, revert root hash and imcyclemax lie in hashed ranges at the manual's documented addresses (the system-architecture slice, not mine). Store/load and shared persistence of the hash tree described at manual 4435-4453 (covered by earlier R9/O1/O2 candidates).

Not covered: Dave LibMachineValidityProof / cartesi-rollups-contracts handling of proof address and size (only noted that game-output.lua binds them); the 'Hash-view of outputs' section after line 8569.
